newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Troops block Zaire protest, man Kinshasa hotspots.
newsitem.headline: Troops block Zaire protest, man Kinshasa hotspots.

text.p: Hundreds of soldiers manned opposition hotspots in Zaire's capital Kinshasa on Friday after dispersing opposition militants trying to gather for a march in the city centre.

Witnesses said the secretary-general of the radical Union for Democracy and Social Progress (UDPS) party, Adrien Phongo, was beaten and arrested by soldiers from the civil guard. The UDPS has called for talks with rebels advancing in the east.
"They arrested the secretary-general, Mr Phongo. They hit him with a truncheon and took him away," said Lofudu Cosmos, a UDPS leader from the swarming working class suburb of Matete.
Three other leading UDPS member were arrested, witnesses said. There was no official confirmation of the arrests.

Armed units of the Civil Guard deployed at corners all along the route of a planned UDPS march, which was due to leave the central train station. Only a few dozen would-be marchers succeeded in reaching the departure point.
Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo's spokesman, Pascale Dema, said troops had been deployed to prevent the march, called in defiance of last month's government ban on all demonstrations.
"It was a provocation. The government has banned all demonstrations during the state of emergency and until the end of the war with (rebel leader Laurent) Kabila," he said.
Laurent Mbayo, a senior adviser of UDPS leader Etienne Tshisekedi, said the march was organised to demand negotiations between Tshisekedi, Kabila and ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko.
UDPS militas in the working class Matonge district said they planned to march to demand the resignation of Kengo and Mobutu, who is at his villa in the south of France.

Mobutu underwent prostate cancer surgery in Europe in August followed by radiation treatment but returned home in December to reshuffle the army and government to respond to the rebel threat in the east. He has since returned twice to Europe.
Aides say there is no cause for concern over his health but the timing of his return to Zaire is unclear.

The Tutsi-led rebels took up arms in October accusing the Zairean authorities of denying them citizenship and planning to expel them to Rwanda, their ancestral home. They hold towns and territory in the east.
They responded to a much-heralded January 20 government counter-offensive by attacking on several fronts, advancing into the mineral-producing southern province of Shaba and pushing north and west.

They have pushed as far west as Kindu and say they are poised to attack Zaire's third city of Kisangani, strategically placed on the Zaire River and headquarters of the army's operations in the war zone.
Zaire accuses Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi of invading in support of the rebels. All deny the charge.

Hope Kivengere, spokeswoman for Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni, told Reuters on Friday that Uganda had no troops in eastern Zaire and French allegations to that effect were "ridiculous and strange".
The rebels demand talks with Mobutu on his departure. Zaire rejects that out of hand. The rebels say a March 19 regional summit in Kenya, which excludes them, will achieve nothing.
